Name: Kryptonis
Description:
Kryptonis is building the computational stack for rocket propulsion.

Today, designing a rocket engine remains a slow and fragmented process. Engineers move between thermodynamic calculations, CAD design, CFD analysis, heat transfer simulations, and structural validation across multiple tools and workflows. A single design iteration can take months before a concept is validated.

We believe propulsion engineering should operate at the speed of computation.

Kryptonis integrates physics-driven modeling, multiphysics simulation, optimization, and intelligent design workflows into a unified computational environment. Instead of treating rocket engines as geometry problems, we begin with the underlying physics and allow validated designs to emerge from it.

Our long-term vision is simple: an engineer should be able to define a mission objective and rapidly explore propulsion architectures, performance trade-offs, and manufacturable engine designs without spending months navigating disconnected software stacks.

We're not replacing engineers.

We're giving them the computational tools to solve harder problems, iterate faster, and build the next generation of propulsion systems.

Engineering at the Speed of Computation.

Mission

These aren't research directions — they are production capabilities, refined by deployment and continuously advanced by an active internal research program.

OrbitIQ Labs operates as both a product company and a research institution. We publish peer-reviewed work, author technical books, and contribute to the scientific foundations of Earth observation and geospatial AI. Every capability we ship is also a capability we study. That feedback loop — between deployment and research — is what keeps our systems ahead of the field.

We work on problems that require genuine depth: signal processing under adversarial conditions, geospatial reasoning at scale, and machine learning architectures designed for the constraints of satellite-derived data. Our output is measured in mission outcomes, not benchmarks.

If you are building in the EO stack, procuring geospatial intelligence, or exploring what satellite data can actually do for your operations — we are worth talking to.

From space to decisions.

Name: Inorbii
Description:
Inorbii is building orbital data center infrastructure—a new tier of compute, engineered to live above the atmosphere.

THE PROBLEM
AI-scale compute is colliding with the physical limits of Earth. Power interconnect queues are measured in years. Cooling consumes ~40% of data center energy and increasingly stresses local water and grids. Hyperscale builds face permitting horizons of 5–10 years. Global data center electricity demand is projected to grow ~1.6× by 2030. These are not marketing narratives; they are engineering ceilings.

THE THESIS
Some workloads—frontier AI training, batch inference, scientific simulation, and sovereign and archival compute—are latency-tolerant and power-hungry. For this class of workload, orbit is a materially different trade space: near-continuous solar generation, radiative heat rejection into the background of space, and zero terrestrial footprint for land, water, and community. Not a replacement for Earth data centers—a complementary layer, purpose-built for compute that benefits from orbital physics.

THE PLATFORM
One modular payload. Three tightly coupled subsystems—solar generation, compute, and radiative cooling—engineered as a single serviceable platform deployed in low-Earth orbit (550–700 km), operated from the ground, and designed for incremental upgrade.

ENGINEERING REALISM
We take seriously the problems space doesn't solve: launch economics, ionising radiation, in-orbit servicing, latency, debris. Modularity, graceful degradation, and rad-hard design are core to the architecture, not afterthoughts.

ROADMAP
Horizon 01—Foundations: subsystem engineering, mission architecture, aerospace, and HPC partnerships. Horizon 02 — Demonstrator: on-orbit validation of the integrated payload. Horizon 03 — Platform: scaling to a production orbital compute fleet for selected workloads.

SpaceTaxi’s work is centered on long-term space mobility, reusable systems, and the physical infrastructure required to make space activity more frequent, reliable, and sustainable.

Name: VSSC/ISRO Technology Transfers
Description:
The Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), located in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, serves as the lead center for the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in the design and development of launch vehicle technology. The center engages in active research across various domains, including aerodynamics, avionics, materials, mechanisms, vehicle integration, chemicals, propulsion, space ordnance, structures, space physics, and systems reliability. 

Under the directives of the Indian Space Policy, ISRO developed technologies are increasingly being commercialised. Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center (IN-SPACe) and NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) have been authorized to enter into Technology Transfer Agreements with suitable entrepreneurs and industries in India. 

VSSC has developed a range of indigenous technologies with applications in both the space sector and various spin-off industries. These include advancements in chemicals, materials, processes, electronics, and software. Many of these technologies have already been transferred to multiple industries and remain available for further collaboration.

To explore the list of available technologies and learn more about the application process, interested parties are encouraged to apply through the IN-SPACe portal.

Contact ttic@vssc.gov.in for further details.

Building the Autonomous Ground Segment

Ground infrastructure is becoming the bottleneck of the space economy.

As constellations grow and missions multiply, operators are expected to run more antennas, more passes, and more networks without growing their teams at the same pace. The ground segment was built to be monitored. It now needs to be autonomous.

ArtemysX is building the Autonomous Ground Segment Platform - the intelligence layer for satellite ground stations, TT&C networks, defence communications and telecom infrastructure.

Autonomous agents run the station end to end: scheduling passes, predicting failures weeks ahead, and monitoring fleet health. And they do the hardest thing in the stack - hold the link when the spectrum is contested, detecting jamming and spoofing and reconfiguring at machine speed, within operator-defined limits and under full operator override.

For commercial satellite and ground station operators, this means higher asset utilisation and more billable passes from infrastructure they already own. For defence, it means links that survive electronic warfare, where a jammed pass is a mission failure. For telecom, it means networks that run leaner and recover faster.
The operator stays in command - supervising, not reacting.

We're transforming the ground segment from a collection of monitored assets into an autonomous operational system.

Industries:
Space Technology
Defence Technology
Telecommunications

Founded by researchers and engineers from NTU Singapore and IIM Kozhikode, ArtemysX is incubated at CODISSIA Defence Innovation and Atal Incubation Centre (CDIIC) - India's First Defence and Innovation hub (Supported by MoD (Ministry of Defence)) and IIMK LIVE, IIM Kozhikode.

Its growing infrastructure includes advanced analog habitats, mission control systems, and upcoming modules focused on bioregenerative life support and human health and performance.

In parallel, AAKA runs analog astronaut training programs, preparing individuals to operate in extreme, mission-critical environments while contributing to real research and data generation.

With India being the world’s most populated country, AAKA is uniquely positioned to build one of the most diverse human performance datasets globally—unlocking insights for the future of long-duration space missions.

Farmonaut delivers satellite intelligence through its Android, iOS, and web platforms, monitoring lakhs of hectares globally and empowering users with actionable insights.

 Agriculture

The platform delivers updates every 3–5 days, including vegetation health, water stress, evapotranspiration, soil organic carbon, and localized weather data. Using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), Farmonaut ensures reliable monitoring even during cloudy conditions.

Its ecosystem also simplifies geotagging and field management, allowing seamless mapping via mobile apps and centralized monitoring through a web dashboard.

 Mining

Farmonaut extends its capabilities to satellite-based mineral exploration, using data from sources like Sentinel, Landsat, and ASTER combined with AI-driven analytics.

Key features include:

Detection of minerals such as gold, lithium, copper, iron, and rare earth elements
Identification of hydrothermal alteration zones and geological structures
AI-powered prospectivity mapping and mineral heatmaps
3D visualization and drill target identification
 Value
Reduce exploration time by up to 90%
Cut costs by 80–85%
Enable non-invasive, scalable, and data-driven decision-making

Farmonaut offers a unified platform for agriculture, mining, and environmental intelligence, helping users optimize resources and improve outcomes globally.

We have six subsystems focused on acquiring competency in their respective sectors for efficient working.

The basic skeleton of the rover is provided by the Mechanical Design & Manufacturing subsystem, which includes the wheels, suspension, chassis, robotic manipulator, and the science module. 

The AI & Automation subsystem processes and interprets data from various sensors such as cameras, GPS, LiDARS, and IMUs. 

The Electronics & Controls subsystem is in charge of powering various segments of the rover, which work together to achieve the rover's desired performance in all tasks for effective control and communication.


The Life science subsystem is in charge of conducting a comprehensive analysis of biological, geological, and chemical features, based on which conclusions about the presence of extinct or extant life can be reached. 

The Research subsystem maintains a portfolio of projects driven by fundamental research and new product innovation. We work not only on great ideas but also implement, deploy, experiment, contribute to and learn from the world around us. We have an outstanding rate of publishing papers and have presented our work at some of the world's top conferences like NAACL and IEEE access.


The management & pr subsystem is responsible for ensuring proper management of the finances, public relations, and logistics of the project along with ensuring efficient communication within its members delegated into its technical subsystems.

Description:
Ulugh Beg Astronomical Institute (UBAI) of the Uzbek Academy of Sciences is the oldest scientific institution not only in Uzbekistan but in the whole Central Asia as well. It was founded as Tashkent Astronomical observatory in 1873 and reorganized to UBAI in 1966. It was known as an important astrometric center of the FSU. The photographic plate collection obtained with the Normal astrograph installed in Tashkent in 1895 and continued up to the mid of the 80s of the last century with Kitab double astrograph made by Zeiss is one of the richest in the world. Since the end of the 19th century UBAI was involved to the International Latitude Service. Kitab station of UBAI was one of five stations of the ILS network. Today Kitab is hosting the ground based beacon of the GPS satellite navigation system.

At present the researches carried out in UBAI are mostly based on the observational data obtained at Maidanak astronomical observatory, located at a distance of 120 km south of the famous historical city of Samarkand. It lies on the spurs of the Pamir and Alai mountain system at 2700 m above the sea level. Maidanak observatory is unique due to its geographical location at the mid distance between the main astronomical facilities on the Canaries and the Hawaii as well as to its high quality atmospheric conditions. It makes Maidanak a very critical site for continuous monitoring of astrophysical objects.

Name: SpaceBelief
Description: Space Belief is replacing heavy aerospace metals with lightweight, bio-engineered materials grown in automated systems.  Traditional satellites and spacecraft rely on heavy metals like aluminum, steel, and lead. These traditional materials add massive weight, costing satellite operators tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars in unnecessary launch fees while offering rigid, hard-to-manufacture structures.  We eliminate these weight penalties and supply chain bottlenecks by growing ultra-lightweight biological composites. Inspired by natural proteins like spider silk, our bio-materials deliver high strength and radiation protection at a fraction of the weight.  What We DoOver 50% Mass Reduction: Our bio-composites are over half the weight of traditional aluminum while delivering 5x the strength-to-weight ratio of steel.  Superior Cosmic Radiation Protection: Hydrogen-rich bio-materials absorb space radiation safely, protecting sensitive satellite electronics without generating dangerous secondary radiation.  Massive Launch Savings: Cutting shielding and structural weight saves satellite operators $42,000 to $500,000+ per spacecraft in launch costs.  Sustainable Biomanufacturing: Conformal, sprayable, and 3D-printable materials that remove reliance on expensive, hard-to-source metals.  Our Vision: Sustainable Space OperationsStarting with high-value satellite panel replacement, Space Belief is laying the foundation for long-term space exploration. By combining automated biomanufacturing with eco-friendly materials, we are building the non-invasive, sustainable infrastructure needed for satellites in Earth orbit and future habitats on the Moon.

Name: STARC Lab
Description:
STARC Lab (Space Technology and Radio Cosmology Laboratory) is a multidisciplinary research group within the Department of Astronomy, Astrophysics and Space Engineering (DAASE), Indian Institute of Technology Indore, led by Prof. Abhirup Datta.

Our research focuses on the development and application of radio astronomy and space-science technologies to address key scientific questions related to the Universe, heliosphere, and near-Earth space environment. The lab integrates theory, observations, instrumentation, and data analysis, with strong expertise in both ground-based and space-based systems.

 Core Research Areas

Radio Astronomy & Radio Cosmology (including low-frequency and 21-cm science)

Space Weather & Ionospheric Physics

Space Technology & Scientific Instrumentation

Radio Interferometry, Calibration, and Signal Processing

Data Analysis, Astrostatistics, and Machine Learning Applications

 Our Mission

Advance fundamental research in astronomy, astrophysics, and space science

Develop innovative instrumentation and analysis techniques for space and ground missions

Foster interdisciplinary collaboration across science and engineering

Train students and early-career researchers through hands-on research and mentoring

STARC Lab is committed to conducting impact-driven research, contributing to national and international collaborations, and nurturing the next generation of scientists and engineers in space science and technology.

Sky1 changes that with an integrated stack: an AI-powered Ground Control System (GCS) on the ground and a compact AI Drone Module on the airframe, enabling autonomous decisions, BVLOS readiness and resilience even in GNSS-denied environments.

Team AIRAVAT aims to advance student-led innovation in aerospace and robotics while building practical, future-ready engineering capabilities through experiential learning.

Name: ISRO Headquarters
Description:
Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is the space agency of India. The organisation is involved in science, engineering and technology to harvest the benefits of outer space for India and the mankind. ISRO is a major constituent of the Department of Space (DOS), Government of India. The department executes the Indian Space Programme primarily through various Centres or units within ISRO.

ISRO was previously the Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR), set up by the Government of India in 1962, as envisioned by Dr. VikramA Sarabhai. ISRO was formed on August 15, 1969 and superseded INCOSPAR with an expanded role to harness space technology. DOS was set up and ISRO was brought under DOS in 1972.

The prime objective of ISRO/DOS is the development and application of space technology for various national needs. To fulfil this objective, ISRO has established major space systemsfor communication, television broadcasting and meteorological services; resources monitoring and management; space-based navigation services. ISRO has developed satellite launch vehicles, PSLV and GSLV, to place the satellites in the required orbits.

Alongside its technological advancement, ISRO contributes to science and science education in the country. Various dedicated research centres and autonomous institutions for remote sensing, astronomy and astrophysics, atmospheric sciences and space sciences in general function under the aegis of Department of Space. ISRO's own Lunar and interplanetary missions along with other scientific projects encourage and promote science education, apart from providing valuable data to the scientific community which in turn enriches science.

Name: HawkLogic Systems
Description:
HawkLogic Systems is a deep-tech spacecraft-engineering company in Bangalore, India, building the tools and flight software that carry a satellite mission from first sketch to orbit.

We start where every mission starts — the numbers. Our free, in-browser mission-design calculators (twenty and counting) answer the questions satellite teams ask first: power and link budgets, delta-v, drag and orbital decay, thermal, radiation, and FCC / ESA debris-compliance — each grounded in cited references (SMAD, ESA, NASA), no login, no backend.

ENKI, our AI spacecraft-design studio, goes further. Describe a CubeSat or small satellite in plain language and ENKI sizes the whole mission with you — running those same calculators as tools, tracking a live design state, sketching the bus in 3D, and explaining every number. It is the fastest path from a rough idea to a sized, sanity-checked design.

ICARUS OS is our flight-software platform for CubeSats: a deterministic, hard-real-time onboard-computer (OBC) operating system with a custom Real-Time Operating System (RTOS), CCSDS-standard telecommand and telemetry, five-level autonomous fault recovery (FDIR), and hardware-level task isolation — in roughly a third of the codebase of comparable frameworks. The kernel is open source.

The through-line is trust: every figure we publish is engineering you can verify, not marketing math — first-order screening to move fast early, backed by references you can check.

DPIIT-recognized. Built in Bangalore, for satellite teams everywhere.

→ Run the calculators and design with ENKI at hawklogicsystems.com
